slides.texte_overlay:
How to command respect
with a calm voice
Speak from your chest, not your throat. A lower, relaxed voice carries authority. Take a breath before you speak and let your words come out slowly.
Say people's names when you disagree. "Mark, I see it differently." Using a name keeps the tone personal and respectful, and it makes people listen.
Never repeat yourself louder. If you're not heard, say it again at the same calm volume. Raising your voice signals to everyone that you've lost control.
Keep your sentences short in tense moments. Long speeches sound defensive. "That's not okay. Let's fix it." Few words, calmly said, carry real weight.
Before: I lost every heated discussion. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calmer, clearer head that keeps my voice steady.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I lost every heated discussion. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A calmer head keeps my voice steady.

slides.texte_overlay: Hold eye contact at the end of your point. Don't look away the second you stop talking. A steady look tells people you mean every word you just said.
Smile when it's over. Once the issue is solved, move on warmly. Calm authority with no grudges is what makes people respect you in the long run.
